sn2.8:1.2: While Pañcālacaṇḍa might be a brahmin teacher, Tāyana (“defender”) is identified as a former religious founder (_purāṇatitthakara_). Indra is sometimes styled “defender” (eg. Rig Veda 2.23.8, 6.25.7).
sn2.8:2.1: These verses are often recited by mendicants to remind them of their commitment.
sn2.8:2.4: As, for example, the gods of universal beauty ([an7.44:4.1]()). This shows Tāyana taught rebirth in the Brahmā realm as the goal of his spiritual life, as did other religious founders of the past ([an6.54](), [an7.73](), [an7.74](), [an7.66]()).
